title: Thunderbird reinstall, cannot connect to recent profile. Appears to have installed in two locations.
creator: amos_shuttlecake
content:
Hi, hoping someone could help as I am struggling to get my information back. I am using Ubuntu Cinnamon.

Thunderbird crashed last night, wouldn't work, tried safe mode. Nothing fixed it. It hung when opening up and after 30 seconds said force quit. So I was forced to reinstall. I did a manual backup but not using the inbuilt tool as I couldn't get into Thunderbird. I just copied the data from username/.thunderbird

After spending a long time uninstalling. Because it reached 78% and then crashed on uninstall. Eventually after reading various pages on the internet I managed to reinstall from the Ubuntu software manager using the latest snap version. (Which I am not sure was what was actually installed previously).

However having used thunderbird for nearly 20 years or so. I have a username/.thunderbird folder. And when I moved to this platform, I have a snap/thunderbird/common/.thunderbird folder.

I installed this new distro 2 years ago, and remember having issues getting my data into the system under Snap. But eventually got it to work somehow back then.

However since reinstalling I cannot see the last 2 years of emails, archives or data. It has launched into a 2 year old profile. I appear to have lost most of the emails from the archive folders (but kept the folders) removed all of the personal folders but then dumped all those emails into my inbox. Giving me 6500 emails that were in various personal folders. (I don't get 6500 emails in a year so don't know what has happened.) It has even changed all of the new dates to the US format, so nothing makes any sense.

I now have 2 Thunderbird profiles, over 12GB in size. And have apparently lost 2 years of my life. But reading support pages, suggests I should be okay because thunderbird doesn't delete data when you reinstall?

I have looked through various other threads which talk about pointing it at the profiles and mail boxes, however nothing works.

Any help much needed.

title: The new Account Hub hiding the password field breaks email setup and is highly frustrating
creator: arno.erasmus1
content: I am writing to express my frustration with the new Account Hub interface in Thunderbird. Specifically, the decision to remove the password field from the initial setup screen is a massive downgrade in user experience.While I understand this was likely designed to accommodate OAuth2 and web-popup logins, it completely breaks down for users setting up accounts with custom domains or standard IMAP/SMTP authentication.Because the password field is hidden upfront, Thunderbird successfully connected to my incoming mail server but completely failed to save or authenticate my outgoing (SMTP) server settings. I spent hours troubleshooting a "cannot find server" error, only to realize the root cause was that the Account Hub never gave me a place to input my password for the outgoing server.Hiding core credentials like passwords doesn't make the app "simpler"—it makes troubleshooting invisible errors a nightmare for users. Please consider bringing back the standard password input field on the very first setup screen, or at least making it optional for manual configurations. My current blocker is I've tried to disable the Account Hub in my settings just to make Thunderbird usable but it is bot changing back to the old add new mail account screen. Please help.
